name: GET /api/leadflow/calendar/readiness - who may receive leads
description:
The SOP §09 calendar checklist, as a GATE rather than a dashboard (2fc627e9-9a59-4d21-ad5e-b7301b6d1990#AC1). Routing a live enquiry to a rep whose booking link is broken converts it into a dead one, and nobody finds out until the prospect gives up - so may_receive_leads is a computed verdict the routing engine can consult, not a number somebody reads on a screen.

EIGHT CHECKS REPORTED SEPARATELY, because each fails for a different reason and is fixed by a different person. A single ready flag tells a manager to "fix the calendar", which is not an instruction anybody can act on; failing[] names exactly which ones are outstanding.

TWO-WAY SYNC IS VERIFIED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS (2fc627e9-9a59-4d21-ad5e-b7301b6d1990#AC2). A connection that READS the calendar but cannot WRITE books meetings nobody sees; one that writes but cannot read double-books over existing commitments. Both are checked and the flag is their conjunction, because a single "connected" hides both failures.

FOUR MEETING TYPES WITH THEIR BUFFERS (2fc627e9-9a59-4d21-ad5e-b7301b6d1990#AC4), verified live: fit_call 15m+5, demo 30m+10, decision_review 30m+10, onboarding 60m+15. The buffer is part of the type rather than a global setting, because a 60-minute onboarding needs more recovery time than a 15-minute fit call.

THE REMINDER LADDER IS RETURNED ALONGSIDE, so an operator can see that the 15-minute rung is internal before they wonder why the customer never got it. QA: depends on register and login.

testCases.name: The checklist reports each check and whether the rep may receive leads
NEGATIVE: no Authorization header at all
NEGATIVE: a bearer token that does not verify

errorCases.message: Authorization header with a bearer token is required
errorCases.when: the Authorization header is absent, empty, or uses a scheme other than Bearer.

errorCases.message: Session token is invalid or expired
errorCases.when: a Bearer token was presented but does not verify.
